description: Verify that DUT does NOT answer ARP Requests for arbitrary 169.254/16 addresses it has not claimed (RFC 3927 §2.7, MUST)
approach:
[Objective]
RFC 3927 §2.7 says a host MUST only respond to ARP Requests targeting the Link-Local address it has actually claimed. This case proves DUT correctly ignores Requests for some other (uninvolved) 169.254/16 address — i.e. it doesn't blanket-answer every Link-Local target as if the whole prefix were its own.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: OpStartLLAutoconf (kicks the Link-Local state machine)

2. DUT: 3 Probes → 2 Announces → claim done. The post-claim observer fires on Listening_post_claim entry, AFTER both Announces have flown. The 2-announce gate matches the spec step-8 wait '(PROBE_MAX*2) + ANNOUNCE_WAIT + ANNOUNCE_INTERVAL', ensuring the inject lands strictly after claim.

3. Tester → DUT: ARP Request with target_proto_ip = an arbitrary 169.254/16 address that is NOT what DUT claimed.

4. Observation (post-claim absence window):
   • DUT must NOT emit any ARP Reply for the arbitrary target

[Pass condition]
DUT performs the 3-probe + 2-announce claim AND emits no ARP Reply for the arbitrary 169.254/16 target.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_no_claim_observed — DUT never announced its committed Link-Local address
• Fail_only_one_announce — fewer than 2 ARP Announces within the deadline
• Fail_responded_to_arbitrary — DUT emitted an ARP Reply for an arbitrary 169.254/16 target it had not claimed

verdicts.Pass: DUT ignored an arbitrary-target Link-Local ARP Request — normal
verdicts.Fail_no_claim_observed: DUT did not announce its committed Link-Local address
verdicts.Fail_only_one_announce: Fewer than 2 ARP Announces within the deadline
verdicts.Fail_responded_to_arbitrary: DUT replied to an ARP Request for a Link-Local address it had not claimed
